stem: Assume each prescription is otherwise valid and the pharmacist has completed all required training. Which Massachusetts pharmacist-administration scenarios fall within a current authorized category? Select all that apply.
choices: Administer prescribed testosterone cypionate for gender-affirming care
Gender-affirming testosterone is an express administration category.
Administer patient-specific Vivitrol for substance use disorder under the applicable prescriber-directed guidance
Extended-release naltrexone is an eligible SUD product.
Administer patient-specific Abilify Maintena for mental illness under the applicable guidance
The listed LAI pathway covers this product.
Administer testosterone cypionate for routine hypogonadism solely because the same product is authorized for gender-affirming care
The statutory indication matters.
Administer insulin glargine for diabetes solely because it is a prescription Schedule VI product
Schedule VI status alone creates no general injection authority.
steps: Match product/indication to a current administration pathway
core: Massachusetts pharmacist administration is driven by an authorized product/indication pathway, not by prescription status alone.
facts: MH/SUD products remain subject to the detailed administration guidance.
trap: Recognizing an injectable product but ignoring the legally material indication.
distinct: Cross-category administration matrix absent from the current bank.
anti_guess: Injectability is shared across options, so product/indication must be evaluated.

stem: Which products are on the Massachusetts pharmacist/pharmacy-intern administration list for treatment of mental illness or substance use disorder, assuming the remaining guidance conditions are met? Select all that apply.
choices: Abilify Maintena (aripiprazole long-acting injection)
Aripiprazole LAI is listed.
Invega Sustenna (paliperidone palmitate)
Paliperidone palmitate LAI is listed.
Vivitrol (extended-release naltrexone)
Vivitrol is the listed SUD injectable.
Lantus (insulin glargine)
Insulin is not on the MH/SUD list.
Testosterone cypionate
Testosterone has a separate statutory administration category, not this MH/SUD list.
steps: Match it to the official MH/SUD administration list
core: The MH/SUD pathway uses a defined list of LAI antipsychotics plus extended-release naltrexone rather than any injectable prescription product.
facts: Other listed antipsychotics include haloperidol decanoate and risperidone long-acting injection.
trap: Selecting an injectable merely because pharmacists may administer it under some other law.
distinct: Product-list burden is new; Q0146 tests prescriber direction instead.
anti_guess: All five are plausible chronic injectable therapies.

stem: A trained Massachusetts pharmacist has a patient-specific prescription for one dose of Vivitrol for substance use disorder, the product is supplied in its single-dose presentation, and the prescriber directs pharmacy administration. What is the best legal characterization?
choices: This can fit the Massachusetts MH/SUD pharmacist-administration pathway when the remaining guidance requirements are met.
Vivitrol is an eligible product under those conditions.
Vivitrol can never be administered by a pharmacist because it treats substance use disorder.
It is expressly listed for this pathway.
The pharmacist may administer any quantity from non-patient-specific bulk stock without a prescription.
The pathway is patient-specific and prescribed.
The product becomes Schedule II when administered in a pharmacy.
Administration location does not reclassify naltrexone.
Only a pharmacy technician may administer this product in Massachusetts.
The pathway is for pharmacists/pharmacy interns, not technicians.
steps: Identify Vivitrol as listed SUD medication
Confirm patient-specific single-dose and prescriber direction
core: Patient-specific, prescribed single-dose Vivitrol can fit Massachusetts pharmacist administration for SUD when all guidance conditions are met.
facts: Prescriber reassessment responsibilities remain part of the treatment relationship.
trap: Assuming a medication used for SUD cannot be pharmacy-administered.
distinct: Real-product application of the MH/SUD pathway.
anti_guess: Distractors preserve the same product while changing authority or classification.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist receives several prescriptions for testosterone cypionate. Which scenarios fit the current statutory pharmacist-administration category specifically because of the indication? Select all that apply.
choices: A prescribed dose for gender-affirming care
That indication is expressly included.
A subsequent prescribed gender-affirming dose after the pharmacist verifies the same authorized pathway remains satisfied
The category is indication-based, not limited to a single first dose.
A prescribed dose for routine testosterone-replacement therapy for hypogonadism, relying only on the gender-affirming statute
That is a different indication.
A bodybuilding request with no valid prescription
Neither indication nor prescription authority is satisfied.
A veterinarian's testosterone order for an animal, relying on the human gender-affirming administration provision
The cited human pharmacist-administration category does not fit.
steps: Classify the indication for each scenario
core: For this pharmacist-administration authority, gender-affirming indication is legally material even though the testosterone product is unchanged.
facts: Testosterone remains federally Schedule III regardless of this administration category.
trap: Letting one authorized use of a drug create blanket administration authority for all uses.
distinct: Q0041 tests testosterone quantity; this tests indication-driven administration.
anti_guess: Every option uses testosterone, eliminating schedule-only guessing.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist administers a patient-specific dose of Abilify Maintena under the mental-illness pathway. Which actions are consistent with the administration guidance? Select all that apply.
choices: Document the administration in the pharmacy's patient record
The administration must be traceable.
Provide required administration information back to the prescriber so the treatment relationship can be maintained
Prescriber communication supports reassessment.
Maintain patient privacy while performing and documenting the injection
Privacy duties remain applicable.
Treat the injection as anonymous floor stock because the product is long acting
The pathway is patient-specific.
Delegate the injection to an unlicensed cashier after the pharmacist confirms the drug
The pharmacist/intern authority is not a cashier delegation pathway.
steps: Apply record, prescriber-communication, and privacy duties
core: Pharmacy administration of an eligible LAI remains patient-specific, documented, and connected to the prescriber.
facts: The guidance does not remove ordinary pharmacy privacy duties.
trap: Copying a loose retail-immunization workflow without the MH/SUD safeguards.
distinct: Post-administration real-drug workflow, not product eligibility.
anti_guess: Each choice is a plausible operational step after an injection.

stem: Each prescription below is for doxycycline intended for an untreated sex partner who has not been examined. Which scenarios fit the Massachusetts pharmacy EPT policy's diagnosis scope? Select all that apply.
choices: The index patient has confirmed chlamydia and a separate partner prescription is issued
Chlamydia fits the EPT policy.
The index patient has chlamydia and the partner prescription uses an accepted EPT designation
That remains within the chlamydia pathway.
The index patient has chlamydia and the partner is named on the separate prescription
Named-partner EPT is allowed.
The index patient has gonorrhea only and the prescription relies solely on Policy 2020-08
The pharmacy policy is chlamydia-only.
The index patient has syphilis only and the prescription relies solely on Policy 2020-08
That diagnosis is outside this EPT policy.
core: Under this Massachusetts pharmacy policy, doxycycline can follow EPT only when the chlamydia EPT pathway is actually triggered.
facts: The drug name alone does not establish EPT eligibility.
trap: Assuming an antibiotic commonly used for STIs makes every STI an EPT case.
distinct: Drug+diagnosis pathway rather than Q0141's abstract condition question.
anti_guess: Same drug appears in every option, so diagnosis must be known.

stem: A valid Massachusetts doxycycline prescription for a chlamydia partner uses 'EPT' in place of the partner's name and address. The pharmacist will dispense it. Which record setup is appropriate?
choices: Create a separate profile and prescription label using the EPT designation in place of the partner name/address.
That is the anonymous EPT workflow.
Place the partner's doxycycline under the index patient's profile as an extra refill.
The partner prescription is separate.
Dispense the drug with no profile or label because the partner is unnamed.
The policy directs creation of both.
Invent a partner date of birth and legal name to make the software accept the prescription.
The EPT designation is the permitted identifier.
Convert doxycycline to OTC status for this transaction.
EPT does not change prescription status.
core: Anonymous doxycycline EPT still receives a pharmacy profile and label, using the EPT designation as permitted.
facts: The partner prescription remains separate from the index patient's prescription.
trap: Using the index patient's record or skipping the pharmacy record entirely.
distinct: Real-drug downstream workflow.
anti_guess: All choices are plausible workarounds for missing patient identity.

stem: A prescriber treats a patient with confirmed chlamydia and wants separate doxycycline prescriptions for the patient's partners. Which constructions are acceptable under the Massachusetts EPT policy? Select all that apply.
choices: Doxycycline prescription for a known partner using that partner's actual name
Named-partner prescribing is permitted.
Doxycycline prescription using 'Expedited Partner Therapy' instead of partner name/address
The full designation is permitted.
Doxycycline prescription using 'E.P.T.' instead of partner name/address
That abbreviation is accepted.
One doxycycline prescription in the index patient's name with directions to divide the labeled supply among all partners
The policy calls for separate partner prescriptions.
A completely blank patient field with no partner name and no EPT designation
The exception requires an accepted EPT identifier.
core: Doxycycline EPT can use a named partner or an accepted EPT designation, but each partner prescription remains a separate prescription.
facts: The pharmacy later creates the corresponding partner profile/label.
trap: Turning the identity exception into permission for a combined or blank prescription.
distinct: Prescription-construction task with a real EPT drug.
anti_guess: Three valid forms use different wording, preventing position/length shortcuts.

stem: At an eligible hospital ADD, a nationally certified Massachusetts-licensed pharmacy technician is using the narrow pathway that does not require prior pharmacist verification. Assume every product is non-patient-specific, sealed, and transferred with electronic validation. Which drugs can fit that pathway based on schedule/PMP status? Select all that apply.
choices: Warfarin
It is Massachusetts Schedule VI and not a PMP drug.
Insulin glargine
It is Schedule VI and not PMP-reportable.
Doxycycline
It is an ordinary Schedule VI prescription drug and not a PMP drug.
Gabapentin
Gabapentin is excluded as a PMP-reportable Schedule VI drug.
Pregabalin
Pregabalin is federally Schedule V, not Schedule VI.
steps: Apply the non-PMP Schedule VI limitation
core: The no-prior-verification certified-technician shortcut is limited to non-PMP Schedule VI stock; gabapentin and federally controlled drugs fall outside it.
facts: Gabapentin remains Massachusetts Schedule VI despite its PMP reporting status.
trap: Treating every Schedule VI drug as eligible or every prescription drug as Schedule VI.
distinct: Credential+drug classification matrix not present in current bank.
anti_guess: Three ordinary prescriptions compete with a Schedule VI/PMP exception and a Schedule V drug.

stem: A pharmacy technician trainee at an eligible Massachusetts hospital is transporting pharmacist-verified stock into an ADD with required electronic validation. Which drugs fall within the trainee's Schedule III-VI stocking boundary? Select all that apply.
choices: Alprazolam
Schedule IV is within III-VI.
Pregabalin
Schedule V is within III-VI.
Gabapentin
Massachusetts Schedule VI is within the boundary.
Warfarin
Massachusetts Schedule VI is within the boundary.
Methylphenidate
Schedule II is outside the PTT stocking boundary.
steps: Apply the PTT Schedule III-VI boundary
core: A PTT may stock pharmacist-verified Schedule III-VI drugs under the policy but not Schedule II stock.
facts: The work remains under pharmacist direction/supervision despite no direct supervision requirement.
trap: Importing the broader licensed-technician Schedule II-VI authority into the trainee pathway.
distinct: Real-drug application of the PTT inventory exception.
anti_guess: Four plausible controlled/prescription drugs are eligible; the single C-II near-miss is not visually obvious.

stem: A Massachusetts-licensed pharmacy technician who is not a trainee works under pharmacist supervision at an eligible hospital ADD. Which scenarios are allowed under the technician stocking policy? Select all that apply.
choices: Load pharmacist-verified methylphenidate using electronic validation
Licensed non-PTT technicians may stock verified S-II-VI.
Load pharmacist-verified alprazolam using electronic validation
Schedule IV falls within the allowed range.
Remove expired pharmacist-controlled gabapentin stock using electronic validation
Expired S-II-VI removal is allowed.
Load unverified pregabalin based solely on the technician's visual check
This licensed-tech pathway requires pharmacist-verified stock.
Load warfarin at an unaffiliated clinic with no on-site pharmacy by relying only on the technician license
The facility/location prerequisites still apply.
steps: Identify licensed-technician rather than PTT status
core: A licensed non-trainee technician may handle pharmacist-verified Schedule II-VI ADD stock under supervision, but not bypass verification or facility prerequisites.
facts: Electronic validation is part of the permitted stocking/removal workflow.
trap: Believing the broader schedule range also removes pharmacist verification.

anti_guess: Drug schedule, verification, and location each create realistic near-misses.

stem: Each option describes a faxed Schedule II prescription. In which cases may the fax serve as the original under a specific federal exception, assuming all other requirements are satisfied? Select all that apply.

Oxycodone for a hospice patient when the prescription indicates hospice status

Fentanyl to be compounded for direct continuous intravenous infusion

Oxycodone tablets for a routine ambulatory patient with no LTCF, hospice, or qualifying infusion facts
The ordinary fax is not itself the original.

facts: The LTCF exception is not limited to narcotics.

trap: Applying the hospice narcotic requirement to LTCF prescriptions.
distinct: Nonnarcotic C-II setting fork.

stem: A pharmacy will compound fentanyl from a valid Schedule II prescription for direct continuous intravenous infusion to the patient. The prescription arrives by fax. Which statement best applies?

distinct: Formulation-specific real-drug fork.
